result:
PBC #14 is handled and the memo is submitted. Here's where things landed.

**Four of five entries are now fully supported in the ledger.** Each has a vendor bill that agrees exactly on invoice number, date, description and amount:

| Entry | Amount | Support attached |
|---|---|---|
| JE-00237 | $1,850.00 | Pluralsight invoice PL-7781 (DOC-0168) |
| JE-00298 | $2,240.00 | Pinecrest Janitorial invoice PJ-0326 (DOC-0199) |
| JE-00275 | $6,000.00 | Ostrander invoice OC-2026-11 (DOC-0192) + FY2026 engagement letter (DOC-0050), which fixes the interim fee at $6,000 |
| JE-00288 | $4,500.00 | Talentbridge invoice TB-4410 (DOC-0198) |

**JE-00293 (K. Lindqvist consulting, $4,800) is an open item — flagged as EXC-001.** It's a manual cash entry by j.doe that bypassed AP, and there is no invoice, agreement, SOW, or email for Lindqvist anywhere in the system. I matched the bank wire (BT-US-0080) to the entry, since the cash disbursement is real, but I did not attach the bank statement as "support" — it proves money left, not what the services were or that 6520 is the right account. I also deliberately left out the Juniper Data Consulting bill that surfaced on the amount search: same $4,800, but a different vendor, February service, already posted and supported as JE-00198. Handing that to the auditors would be dressing up a coincidence as evidence.

**The memo includes a draft PBC response** that gives Ostrander the four supported items now and discloses Lindqvist as an open item pending documentation from j.doe, rather than sitting on the whole response until the 4/6 deadline. No entries were posted or reversed, and nothing required controller approval.

One thing worth your attention: since this entry went around AP with no document, you may want to spot-check j.doe's other manual cash entries in March for the same pattern.
